title: संशयादिपदार्थविश्लेषणम् [Samshayadipadarthavishleshanam]
nepali: न्यायदर्श नस्य प्रतिपादको महर्षि गौतमो ऽस्ति । न्यायदर्शने विशेषतो ग्रन्थकारेण निःश्रे यसप्राप्तिमार्ग प्रदर्शितो विद्यत । न्यायदर्श नानुसारं पदार्थानां तत्त्वज्ञान नै व मा क्षप्राप्तिर्भ वति । प्रमाणादिषा डशपदार्था नां तत्त्वज्ञानं यथार्थ ज्ञानं वामा क्षस्य मूलमार्गा विद्यते । अतो यमाले खः पदार्थानां मध्ये संशयादिपदार्था नां प्रमाणप्रमे याभ्यां पृथगुपदेशः कारणत्वप्रतिपादने , एतेषां लक्षणविश्ले षणेचकेन्द्रितो विद्यते । अस्मिन्नालेखे सर्व प्रथमं न्यायाभिमतप्रमाणप्रमे ययो स्वरूपनिदर्श नपूर्व कं संशयादिपदार्थ स्वरूपविश्ले षणं क्रियते । प्रमाकरणरूपाणां प्रमाणानां सहयो गितया तदङ्गरूपे ण संशयादिपदार्था नामप्यन्तरभावस्य कर्तु शक्यत्वात् , अथवा प्रमायाः विषयबो धेषुप्रमे येषु मध्ये सर्व मपिसंशयादिपदार्थ जातमन्तर्भू तं भवत्यवेति, कुतः पृ थक्तया सूत्रकारेणो द्दे शः कृ तः ? इति समस्यायाः समाधानार्थ मयं प्रयत्नो वर्तते । सकारणसंशयादिपदार्थो पदे शप्रतिपादने न एतेषां स्वरूपस्य सम्यक्तया विश्लेषणमत्र विहितमस्ति । अन्तचैतेषां प्रमाणप्रमे यादिभ्यः पृथुगुपद्दे शस्य कारणत्वं प्रदश्र्य निष्कर्ष : प्रदत्तो विद्यते । अस्मान्निकर्षा न्न्यायनिर्दि ष्टानां षो डशपदार्था नामध्ययनाध्यापनाय सारल्यं भविते त्यपे क्षते । [The term NyayaDarshan was first introduced by MaharshiGautam. The philosophy NyayaDarshan especially mentions the way to achieve Moksha. The philosophy categorizes each physical and non-physical element in 16 categories known as “Padartha”. According to NyayaDarshan, having the knowledge and perceiving these Padartha in their own original form, is the only way to achieve Moksha. This paper tries to investigate the reasons for separately discussing and defining 14 Padartha other than Praman and Prameya known as Smshayadi in Nyaya Sutra. In the initial section, the brief discussion on Praman and Prameya followed by SamshayadiPadartha of NayaDarshan has been mentioned. Praman being a medium of Prama and Samshayadi being a supportive concept of Praman; as a result Smashayadi itself can be included within Praman. Additionally, as all Smashayadi are Prameya or the subjects of Prama, Smashayadi also can be included within Prameya. We have theoretical evidence that Samshayadipadartha can be included either in Praman or Prameya. Hence, this paper attempts to investigate the question, “Why does Naya Darshan mention the Samshayadi Padartha separately?” The in-depth dialog and reasons for including Samshayadipadartha within the Nyaya Sutra has also been discussed. Article includes the reasons for separating these Padartha from Praman and Prameya and concludes with the expectation of understanding 16 padartha easily for simplifying the teaching-learning process.]
american_english: Maharshi Gautama is the proponent of the Nyaya philosophy. In the Nyaya philosophy, the path to attaining the highest good (nihshreyasa) is especially indicated by the author of the treatise. According to Nyaya philosophy, the attainment of liberation (moksha) occurs solely through the true knowledge (tattvajnana) of the categories (padarthas). True knowledge or accurate understanding of the sixteen categories beginning with the means of valid cognition (pramana) is the primary path to liberation. Hence, this article is focused on establishing the justification for the separate instruction of the categories beginning with doubt (samshaya) apart from pramana and prameya among the categories, and on analyzing their defining characteristics. In this article, first of all, after illustrating the nature of pramana and prameya accepted in Nyaya, an analysis of the nature of the categories beginning with doubt is carried out. Since it would have been possible to subsume the categories beginning with doubt as auxiliaries and limbs of the means of valid cognition serving as instruments of valid knowledge, or since the entire group of categories beginning with doubt is inherently included among the objects of valid cognition (prameyas) in the cognition of the object of valid knowledge, why did the author of the aphorisms enumerate them separately? This effort is undertaken to resolve this problem. Through establishing the reasoned teaching of the categories beginning with doubt, a thorough analysis of their nature is performed here. Finally, by demonstrating the causal justification for their separate instruction apart from pramana, prameya, and the rest, a conclusion is provided. From this conclusion, it is anticipated that there will be ease in the study and teaching of the sixteen categories specified in Nyaya.

informal_english: Maharshi Gautama is the main proponent of Nyaya philosophy. In Nyaya philosophy, the author specifically points out the road to reaching the ultimate good (nihshreyasa). According to Nyaya, scoring liberation (moksha) only happens through the true grasp (tattvajnana) of the categories (padarthas). Having true knowledge or a proper grasp of the sixteen categories starting with the means of valid knowledge (pramana) is the main highway to liberation. So, this article zooms in on explaining why the categories starting with doubt (samshaya) get taught separately from pramana and prameya, and breaking down their definitions. In this paper, first off, after showing what Nyaya means by pramana and prameya, we break down what the doubt-and-company categories are all about. Since categories like doubt could easily just be lumped in as helpers and limbs of the pramanas that produce valid knowledge, or since the whole lot of them actually fits under the knowables (prameyas) as objects of valid cognition, why on earth did the sutra author list them separately? This whole effort is here to sort out that problem. By arguing the case for why these doubt-related categories get taught separately, a proper analysis of what they actually are is dished up here. Finally, by laying out the reasoning behind teaching them apart from pramana, prameya, and the rest, a solid conclusion is given. From this conclusion, the hope is that studying and teaching the sixteen Nyaya categories will become way simpler.
translator_notes: The source text is composed in academic Sanskrit with minor OCR anomalies, followed by an author-provided English summary in square brackets; the Sanskrit text was translated directly sentence by sentence across all 11 sentences, without relying on the bracketed summary as a substitute. Key Nyaya epistemological concepts (न्यायदर्शन / Nyaya philosophy, निःश्रेयस / nihshreyasa, मोक्ष / moksha, तत्त्वज्ञान / tattvajnana, प्रमाण / pramana, प्रमेय / prameya, प्रमा / prama, संशय / samshaya) are translated accurately.
